sections.heading: What Is an Insulated Glass Unit and When Does It Need Replacement?
sections.body: An insulated glass unit, commonly called an IGU, consists of two or more panes of glass sealed together with a spacer and an inert gas fill — typically argon or krypton — in between. This sealed assembly is what gives modern windows their thermal and acoustic performance. Over time, the seal can fail due to age, temperature cycling, moisture infiltration, or physical impact. When the seal breaks down, outside air and humidity enter the gap between the panes, causing the telltale foggy or hazy appearance that no amount of cleaning can fix. You may also notice condensation forming between the panes, distorted views, or drafts near the glass surface. At that point, replacing the IGU itself — rather than the entire window frame — is often the most practical and cost-effective path forward. Our technicians assess each unit carefully to confirm that the frame is sound and that an IGU swap will fully resolve the issue.

sections.heading: Residential Insulated Glass Unit Replacement Throughout Alexandria
sections.body: Homeowners across Alexandria neighborhoods — from Del Ray bungalows to the townhomes and condominiums lining the waterfront near the Torpedo Factory Art Center — frequently encounter IGU failures in aging double-pane windows. A fogged-up window in a living room or bedroom is frustrating, and waiting too long can allow secondary issues like frame moisture damage to develop. Rather than replacing the entire window, which involves significant disruption and expense, our residential IGU replacement service targets only the failed glass unit itself. We measure and order replacement units to match the exact specifications of your existing frames, then install them cleanly and professionally. The result is a clear, properly functioning window that looks and performs like new. We work with a variety of residential window brands and frame materials including vinyl, wood, fiberglass, and aluminum, making us a versatile choice for homeowners throughout the Alexandria area.

sections.heading: How the IGU Replacement Process Works
sections.body: Our replacement process begins with an on-site assessment where a technician measures the failed unit and evaluates the condition of the surrounding frame and glazing system. Accurate measurements are critical — a unit that is even slightly off in size will not seal properly or perform as intended. Once we have confirmed the specifications, we source a replacement IGU matched to your existing setup, including the appropriate glass type, thickness, spacer width, and gas fill. On installation day, our team carefully removes the old unit, cleans the frame channel, and sets the new IGU using the correct glazing tape, setting blocks, and sealant for a weathertight finish. We inspect the completed installation before leaving the site to confirm the unit is properly seated and sealed. The turnaround time varies based on unit size and availability, but we work to complete most residential and light commercial replacements as quickly as possible to minimize inconvenience.

faq.q: How do I know if my window needs an IGU replacement or a full window replacement?
faq.a: If the foggy or failed appearance is confined to the glass itself and the surrounding frame is structurally sound — no rot, warping, or significant damage — an IGU replacement is usually all that is needed. A full window replacement becomes necessary when the frame is compromised or when the entire window system is outdated and no longer functional. Our technicians assess both during the initial site visit and give you a straightforward recommendation.
